answer: Divergent Beacon Registry: each identity must periodically sign a fresh random challenge alongside a secret it alone holds, producing a mildly unique reply—like lighting a lantern that can't be copied. Clones share one secret, so their replies converge. The registry forges a per-identity fingerprint from response timing and drift; identical outputs across supposedly independent agents flag a sybil cluster. To pass, an attacker must run genuinely separate agents, paying full compute and a copper-level hardware cost per identity.
